olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute $\triangle ABC$; $M$ = midpoint of $BC$; $P$ = foot of perpendicular from $C$ to $AM$. Circumcircle of $\triangle ABP$ meets line $BC$ at $B,Q$; $N$ = midpoint of $AQ$. Prove $NB=NC$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2023

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: An $n\times n$ board ($n$ odd) with a maximal grid-aligned configuration $C$ of $(n^2-1)/2$ non-overlapping dominoes. Sliding a domino covers the uncovered square and uncovers another. Let $k(C)$ = number of distinct configurations reachable from $C$ by repeated slides. Find all possible values of $k(C)$ as a function of $n$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2023

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Positive integer $a$ selected; positive integers on a board. Alice adds $a$ to some $n$; Bob halves some even $n$. Alice first, they alternate; if Bob has no valid move, game ends. If Bob can force the game to end, show the game ends regardless of either player's moves.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2023

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $1,\ldots,n^2$ in an $n\times n$ table. Arrangement is row-valid if each row can be permuted to an AP; column-valid if each column can. For which $n$ can any row-valid arrangement be made column-valid by permuting rows?
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2023

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\triangle ABC$ with incenter $I$, excenters $I_a,I_b,I_c$. $D$ on circumcircle not on $II_a$, $I_bI_c$, or $BC$. Circumcircles of $\triangle DII_a$ and $\triangle DI_bI_c$ meet at $D,F$; $E=DF\cap BC$. Prove $\angle BAD=\angle EAC$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2023
